approved: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage (Regulatory Levies) Amendment Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill updates how levies are charged under offshore petroleum and greenhouse gas laws.
It would make the environmental plan levy payable by someone who submits a plan before getting a title, not just after.
The bill also ensures the annual titles administration levy applies even if a title lasts less than a full year or beyond its original term.
The bill extends the environment plan levy to applicants for certain titles who submit a plan before the title is granted.
It makes the levy payable by holders of petroleum scientific investigation consents or greenhouse gas research consents.
It clarifies that annual titles administration levy is imposed for each anniversary of the title's start, even if the title continues past its nominal term or ends early.
Offshore petroleum and greenhouse gas titleholders, applicants for certain titles, and holders of scientific investigation or research consents.

Supported amendments strengthening the offshore petroleum regulator's enforcement powers following lessons from the Montara oil spill in August 2009 and the BP Macondo well disaster in the Gulf of Mexico in April 2010, which killed 11 people, and noted the offshore petroleum industry has contributed nearly $28 billion to the Australian economy.

Supported the offshore petroleum regulatory bills but warned that removing 457 visa market-testing and excluding coastal waters from the migration zone would let operators bring in more foreign labour, citing foreign crews laying pipeline for the Ichthys project in north-west Western Australia.
